এসব কথা উঠে এসেছে বৃহস্পতিবার জাতীয় প্রেসক্লাবে ‘পাহাড়ে অস্থিরতার কারণ ও প্রতিকার’ শীর্ষক এক আলোচনা সভায়।

title: US firms line up investment proposals as DFC delegation plans Bangladesh visit in January
summary: Illustration: TBS A delegation from the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) is expected to visit Bangladesh in January 2027 to assess potential investment projects as several US companies have expressed interest in accessing its financing following the restoration of the country's eligibility.
key_facts: On 16 November, the DFC announced that projects in Bangladesh would once again be eligible for its financing, ending a 13-year suspension imposed in 2013 following the Rana Plaza disaster.
The corporation can provide loans covering up to 50% of a project's total financing requirements.
For equity investments, it can take a maximum 40% stake in a company or project, the officials said.
Loan tenures typically range from three to 15 years, depending on the nature of the investment, while the approval process can take around six to 12 months.

title: DB detains actor Tomal Mahbub for questioning
summary: Photo: Courtesy The Detective Branch (DB) has brought actor Tomal Mahbub to its office for questioning. DB chief Additional Commissioner Shafiqul Islam confirmed the matter around 1am today (20 November).
key_facts: He said Tomal had been brought to the DB office for questioning and that details would be disclosed later.
The time and place of his detention were not immediately known.
While most comments will be posted if they are on-topic and not abusive, moderation decisions are subjective.

title: Borrowers in disputes eligible for Tk60,000cr stimulus loans with court stay orders
summary: Illustration: TBS Borrowers involved in disputes with their lenders will be eligible for loans under Bangladesh Bank's Tk60,000 crore stimulus schemes if they obtain a court stay order suspending loan-related proceedings against them. The central bank issued the directive recently to facilitate the implementation of 15 economic recovery schemes.
key_facts: Other loan disbursements must follow BRPD-1 Circular Letter No 25, issued on 29 July 2026.
The 15 schemes, totalling Tk60,000 crore, cover industries and services, cottage, micro, small and medium enterprises (CMSMEs), agriculture and other employment-generating sectors.
The directive, issued under Section 45 of the Bank Company Act, 1991, takes immediate effect.

title: Global soybean market shifts put Bangladesh's poultry, fish industries on alert
summary: Photo: Courtesy Bangladesh's rapidly expanding poultry and fisheries industries need to pay greater attention to the nutritional quality and reliability of imported soybean meal as geopolitical tensions and shifting global trade routes reshape the international feed market, industry experts have said.
key_facts: The issue came into focus at CrushCON 2026, a global soybean industry conference organised by the US Soybean Export Council (USSEC) for its Middle East, North Africa and South Asia (MENASA) region in Istanbul, Türkiye, on 18 November.
According to export data from the US Department of Agriculture's Foreign Agricultural Service, MENASA countries imported more than 8 million tonnes of US soybeans in the 2025-26 marketing year.
Egypt alone accounted for around 5 million tonnes, while Algeria's imports exceeded 500,000 tonnes in the early part of the 2026-27 marketing year.
Crude protein is estimated by multiplying total nitrogen content by 6.25, but the figure does not directly indicate how much protein animals can digest and utilise.

title: বারিধারা থেকে সাতক্ষীরার সাবেক এমপি আতাউল হক গ্রেপ্তার
summary: সাতক্ষীরা-৪ আসনের সাবেক সংসদ সদস্য এস এম আতাউল হককে (দোলন) গ্রেপ্তার করেছে স্পেশাল রেসপন্স ব্যাটালিয়ন (এসআরবি)। বৃহস্পতিবার দিবাগত রাত সাড়ে ১১টার দিকে রাজধানীর বারিধারার ডিওএইচএস থেকে তাঁকে গ্রেপ্তার করা হয় বলে আইনশৃঙ্খলা–সংশ্লিষ্ট একটি সূত্র জানিয়েছে। আতাউল হক কার্যক্রম নিষিদ্ধ আওয়ামী লীগের সাতক্ষীরার শ্যামনগর উপজেলা শাখার সাধারণ সম্পাদক। তাঁর বাড়ি উপজেলার গুমানতলী গ্রামে। আতাউল হকের বিরুদ্ধে শ্যামনগর থানায় একটি হত্যাসহ সাতটি মামলা রয়েছে বলে সংশ্লিষ্ট সূত্র জানিয়েছে। জুলাই গণ-অভ্যুত্থানে ক্ষমতাচ্যুত সাবেক প্রধানমন্ত্রী শেখ হাসিনার ডিসেম্বরে ফেরার ঘোষণাকে কেন্দ্র করে অনলাইনে কার্যক্রম নিষিদ্ধ
key_facts: আতাউল হকের বিরুদ্ধে শ্যামনগর থানায় একটি হত্যাসহ সাতটি মামলা রয়েছে বলে সংশ্লিষ্ট সূত্র জানিয়েছে।

জুলাই গণ-অভ্যুত্থানে ক্ষমতাচ্যুত সাবেক প্রধানমন্ত্রী শেখ হাসিনার ডিসেম্বরে ফেরার ঘোষণাকে কেন্দ্র করে অনলাইনে কার্যক্রম নিষিদ্ধ দলটির ঘোষিত কর্মসূচি ঘিরে দেশের বিভিন্ন জায়গায় গাড়িতে আগুন ও ককটেল বিস্ফোরণের ঘটনা ঘটছে।
উদ্ভূত পরিস্থিতিতে নতুন করে আওয়ামী লীগ–সংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যক্তিদের গ্রেপ্তারের ঘটনা বেড়েছে।

title: আ.লীগের বিরুদ্ধে মাঠে নামছে এনসিপি, রাজপথ ‘দখলের’ হুঁশিয়ারি
summary: চলমান সহিংস পরিস্থিতির মধ্যে কার্যক্রম নিষিদ্ধ আওয়ামী লীগের বিরুদ্ধে মাঠে নামার ঘোষণা দিয়েছে জাতীয় নাগরিক পার্টি (এনসিপি)। ২৩ নভেম্বর থেকে ৩১ ডিসেম্বর পর্যন্ত রাজধানী ঢাকাসহ দেশের সব জেলা ও মহানগরে ধারাবাহিক বিক্ষোভ ও প্রতিবাদ সভা করবে দলটি। এসব কর্মসূচি হবে ‘গণহত্যাকারী সংগঠন আওয়ামী লীগের বিচার, শেখ হাসিনার ফাঁসির রায় কার্যকর করা, গণহত্যাকারীদের বিচার ত্বরান্বিত করা এবং গঙ্গা চুক্তিতে বাংলাদেশের ন্যায্য হিস্যা আদায়ের দাবিতে’। দলীয় কর্মসূচির পাশাপাশি জামায়াতে ইসলামীর নেতৃত্বাধীন ১১–দলীয় ঐক্যের কর্মসূচিতেও অংশ নেবেন এনসিপির নেতা–কর্মীরা। বৃহস্পতিবার সন্ধ্যায় রাজধানীর বাংলামোটরে দলীয় কার্যালয়ে
key_facts: দলীয় কর্মসূচির পাশাপাশি জামায়াতে ইসলামীর নেতৃত্বাধীন ১১–দলীয় ঐক্যের কর্মসূচিতেও অংশ নেবেন এনসিপির নেতা–কর্মীরা।
দলীয় কর্মসূচির পাশাপাশি ১১ দলের কর্মসূচিতেও এনসিপির অংশগ্রহণ থাকবে।
ভারত সরকার ৫ আগস্টের পর গণহত্যাকারী শেখ হাসিনাকে আশ্রয়-প্রশ্রয় দিয়েছে।

title: ‘তুমিই আমার ছেলের উত্তরসূরি’—নিকো পাজকে মেসির মা
summary: লিওনেল মেসি গত অক্টোবরে অবসর নেওয়ার পর চলতি মাসে দুটি প্রীতি ম্যাচে আর্জেন্টিনার ১০ নম্বর জার্সিতে কাউকে মাঠে দেখা যায়নি। এ জার্সির উত্তরসূরি পরে বেছে নেওয়া হবে বলে জানিয়েছেন আর্জেন্টিনার কোচ লিওনেল স্কালোনি। কিন্তু কেউ কেউ এরই মধ্যে মেসির ১০ নম্বর জার্সিতে দেখছেন নিকো পাজকে। তাঁদের সেই দেখার পালে জোর হাওয়া দিলেন স্বয়ং লিওনেল মেসির মা! পাজের পরিবার জানিয়েছে, গত অক্টোবরে বেনিনের বিপক্ষে প্রীতি ম্যাচে মেসির মা সেলিয়া কুচ্চিত্তিনির সঙ্গে দেখা হয় এই অ্যাটাকিং মিডফিল্ডারের। সেটিই ছিল আর্জেন্টিনার হয়ে মেসির শেষ ম্যাচ। সে ম্যাচে দারুণ এক গোল করে নিজের ‘আইডল’ মেসিকে জড়িয়েও ধরেন পাজ। সেদিন ম্যাচের পর
key_facts: সেদিন ম্যাচের পর মেসির মা পাজকে বলেন, জাতীয় দলে তিনিই হবেন তাঁর ছেলের ১০ নম্বর জার্সির উত্তরসূরি।
মন থেকে ও এখনো একদম শিশুর মতোই সরল।’ ২০২৬ বিশ্বকাপের পর আর্জেন্টিনার জার্সিতে ৫ গোল করেছেন পাজ।
গতকাল সকালে কোস্টারিকার বিপক্ষে বছরের শেষ প্রীতি ম্যাচে ৭–০ গোলের জয়ে জোড়া গোল করেন পাজ।
সে ম্যাচের পর ১০ নম্বর জার্সি নিয়ে ২২ বছর বয়সী মিডফিল্ডার বলেন, ‘এই (আর্জেন্টিনা) জার্সির প্রতিনিধিত্ব করতে পারাটাই সর্বোচ্চ ব্যাপার।

title: Former Satkhira-4 MP Ataul Haque Dolon arrested in Dhaka
summary: Former Satkhira-4 lawmaker Ataul Haque Dolon was arrested yesterday (19 November) in the capital's Baridhara DOHS area. A Special Response Battalion (SRB-1) team arrested him around 11:20pm yesterday (19 November), acting on a tip-off, said MZM Intakhab Chowdhury, director of the unit's Legal and Media Wing. Dolon is a former lawmaker of the Awami League, whose political activities are currently banned.
key_facts: According to case records, a murder case was filed against him at Shyamnagar Police Station on 5 September 2024.
The case includes allegations under sections 302, 427, 379 and 34 of the Penal Code.

Another case, filed on 19 January 2024, concerns alleged violations of Rule 18 of the Representation of the People (Election) Rules, 2008, and Article 73 of the Representation of the People Order, 1972, relating to electoral conduct.
In a case filed on 5 June 2025, Dolon was accused under sections 4 and 6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908, and sections 15(3) and 25(d) of the Special Powers Act, 1974.

title: জগন্নাথ বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ে নিষিদ্ধ ছাত্রলীগের নেতাকে আটক করে পুলিশে দিল ছাত্রদল
summary: নিষিদ্ধঘোষিত সংগঠন ছাত্রলীগের জগন্নাথ বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় শাখার এক নেতাকে আটকের পর মারধর করে কোতোয়ালি থানা–পুলিশের কাছে হস্তান্তর করেছেন বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় শাখা ছাত্রদলের নেতা–কর্মীরা। বৃহস্পতিবার বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের দর্শন বিভাগ থেকে শাকিল খান নামের ওই শিক্ষার্থীকে আটক করা হয়। শাকিল ওই বিভাগের ২০১৯–২০ শিক্ষাবর্ষের শিক্ষার্থী এবং বিভাগীয় শাখা ছাত্রলীগের সাধারণ সম্পাদকের দায়িত্বে ছিলেন। বিভাগীয় সূত্রে জানা যায়, নিষিদ্ধঘোষিত ছাত্রলীগের ওই নেতা বিশ্ব দর্শন দিবস উপলক্ষে আয়োজিত নবীনবরণ ও বিদায় অনুষ্ঠানে ক্যাম্পাসে এসেছিলেন। খবর পেয়ে ছাত্রদলের নেতা–কর্মীরা সেখানে গিয়ে তাঁকে আটক করেন। তখন শাকিলের বন্ধু–সহপাঠীরা তাঁদ
key_facts: শাকিল ওই বিভাগের ২০১৯–২০ শিক্ষাবর্ষের শিক্ষার্থী এবং বিভাগীয় শাখা ছাত্রলীগের সাধারণ সম্পাদকের দায়িত্বে ছিলেন।
বৃহস্পতিবার বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের দর্শন বিভাগ থেকে শাকিল খান নামের ওই শিক্ষার্থীকে আটক করা হয়।
বিভাগীয় সূত্রে জানা যায়, নিষিদ্ধঘোষিত ছাত্রলীগের ওই নেতা বিশ্ব দর্শন দিবস উপলক্ষে আয়োজিত নবীনবরণ ও বিদায় অনুষ্ঠানে ক্যাম্পাসে এসেছিলেন।

title: ১৬ জেলায় নাশকতা, গাড়ি–স্থাপনায় আগুন, লগি–বইঠা জব্দ
summary: গোপালগঞ্জে বিএনপির এমপির বাড়ি ও মুকসুদপুর থানায় হামলা-অগ্নিসংযোগসহ ১৬ জেলায় সরকারি-বেসরকারি স্থাপনা ও যানবাহনে নাশকতার ঘটনা ঘটেছে। সাবেক শিক্ষামন্ত্রীসহ গত ২৪ ঘণ্টায় ঢাকায় গ্রেপ্তার ১০৭ জন। বিস্তারিত ভিডিও প্রতিবেদনে...

title: সুন্দরী প্রতিযোগিতা থেকে চলচ্চিত্রে, রাজনীতি: জ্যোতিকা জ্যোতির যত উত্থান-পতন
summary: সুন্দরী প্রতিযোগিতা দিয়ে শুরু। এরপর টেলিভিশন নাটক, দেশের চলচ্চিত্র পেরিয়ে কলকাতার সিনেমায় অভিনয়। গ্ল্যামারনির্ভর নায়িকা হওয়ার চেয়ে চরিত্রাভিনেত্রী হিসেবেই নিজের জায়গা তৈরি করেছিলেন জ্যোতিকা জ্যোতি। অভিনয়ের দক্ষতায় প্রশংসা পেয়েছেন দুই বাংলায়। পুরস্কারও এসেছে। একসময় অভিনয়ের পাশাপাশি সক্রিয় হন রাজনীতিতে। জাতীয় সংসদ নির্বাচনে কার্যক্রম নিষিদ্ধ আওয়ামী লীগের মনোনয়ন চেয়েছিলেন। পরে সরকারি প্রতিষ্ঠানের পরিচালক পদেও নিয়োগ পান। কিন্তু ২০২৪ সালের রাজনৈতিক পটপরিবর্তনের পর বদলে যেতে থাকে তাঁর জীবন। বিতর্কিত হোয়াটসঅ্যাপ গ্রুপে যুক্ত থাকার অভিযোগ, সরকারি চাকরি হারানো, অভিনয়ে কাজ না পাওয়া—একের পর এক ঘটনায় আলোচ
key_facts: কিন্তু ২০২৪ সালের রাজনৈতিক পটপরিবর্তনের পর বদলে যেতে থাকে তাঁর জীবন।
বুধবার (১৮ নভেম্বর) দিবাগত রাতে রাজধানীর উত্তরার বাসা থেকে জ্যোতিকা জ্যোতিকে গ্রেপ্তার করে ঢাকা মহানগর গোয়েন্দা পুলিশ (ডিবি)।
বিজ্ঞপ্তিতে বলা হয়, গোপন সংবাদের ভিত্তিতে ডিবির উত্তরা বিভাগের একটি দল রাত আড়াইটার দিকে তুরাগ থানাধীন উত্তরার ১৮ নম্বর সেক্টরের একটি বাসায় অভিযান চালিয়ে তাঁকে গ্রেপ্তার করে।
২০০৪ সালে লাক্স–আনন্দধারা ফটোজেনিক প্রতিযোগিতায় সেরা দশে জায়গা করে নেওয়ার মধ্য দিয়ে বিনোদন অঙ্গনে পথচলা শুরু করেন।

title: Ducsu leader's Gopalganj family home vandalised, set on fire
summary: Ducsu Cultural Affairs Secretary Musaddiq Ali Ibne Mohammad's file photo. Dhaka University Central Students' Union (Ducsu) Cultural Affairs Secretary Musaddiq Ali Ibne Mohammad said his ancestral home was attacked, vandalised and looted in Muksudpur upazila of Gopalganj yesterday (19 November). The fire was set in the early hours of the morning, while the vandalism and looting took place around noon, reports Prothom Alo.
key_facts: Speaking to Prothom Alo, Musaddiq said his family lives in Dhaka but regularly visits their ancestral home.
His second-eldest brother has been living there for several years, while his father travels between Dhaka and the village every week.
He said the Awami League, whose political activities are currently banned, had been circulating threats on social media for the past week, warning of an attack on their house.

title: Don't be misled by conspiracies, rumors or propaganda: IGP
summary: Photo: Courtesy Inspector General of Police Md Ali Hossain Fakir has urged citizens not to be misled by conspiracies, rumours or propaganda, assuring them that police are performing their duties professionally and in accordance with the law. He made the remarks on Thursday as the chief guest at the final match and prize-giving ceremony of the Bangladesh Police Volleyball (Men and Women) Championship 2026 at Shaheed Noor Hossain Volleyball Stadium in Gulistan, Dhaka.
key_facts: Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) clinched the men's title by defeating Dhaka Range, while the Armed Police Battalion (APBn) won the women's championship after beating Chattogram Metropolitan Police (CMP).
DMP's Milon and APBn's Keya were named the best players in the men's and women's categories respectively.
Speaking at the ceremony, the IGP described sports as an important means of building a drug-free society and announced initiatives to identify and develop young athletic talent across the country.

title: Bangladesh Bank allows loan defaulters with court stay orders to access Tk 60,000cr stimulus
summary: Star Business Report VISUAL: STAR Bangladesh Bank has relaxed its rules on stimulus loans, allowing borrowers who hold court stay orders against default proceedings to access the Tk 60,000 crore stimulus package. The central bank issued a circular on Thursday in this regard, effective immediately. The Bank Company Act bars banks from extending fresh loans to defaulters.
key_facts: In all other cases, the instructions in the July 29 circular from the Banking Regulation and Policy Department still apply.
By mid-October, banks disbursed about Tk 12,000 crore, a fifth of the total, to help struggling businesses, reopen closed factories and generate jobs.
The circular said the package has 15 special schemes, designed to create direct and indirect employment, revive economic activity, retain workers and help entrepreneurs stay competitive.

The low-interest schemes include refinancing for closed industries and service-sector enterprises, working capital for cottage, micro, small and medium enterprises, and a Tk 3,000 crore fund to develop agro-based special economic hubs in northern Bangladesh.

title: Bangladesh Bank allows loan defaulters with court stay orders to access Tk 60,000 crore stimulus
summary: Central bank relaxes eligibility rules to speed up lending, drawing criticism from bankers and financial sector analysts

title: Amnesty urges Bangladesh to stop arresting garment workers, union leaders
summary: Workers protest in front of an RMG factory in Ashulia on 30 September 2024. Photo: TBS Amnesty International has expressed deep concern over what it described as the targeting of garment workers and trade union leaders in Bangladesh demanding a higher minimum wage, urging authorities to stop arrests and to respect the right to peaceful assembly. The rights watchdog urged authorities to cease harassment and differentiate peaceful protesters from those engaging in violence.
key_facts: The call follows the November 17 detention of Green Bangla Garments Workers Federation (GBGWF) President Sultana Begum and General Secretary Md Elias by Detective Branch police after a webinar on minimum-wage protests.
They allegedly face charges of obstructing police duties and factory vandalism.
While most comments will be posted if they are on-topic and not abusive, moderation decisions are subjective.

title: NCP announces month-long nationwide protests demanding AL trial
summary: National Citizen Party (NCP) hold a press conference at the party's central office in the capital's Banglamotor. The National Citizen Party (NCP) has announced nationwide protests and rallies through December, demanding the trial of the Awami League as an organisation, implementation of the death sentence against ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, and speedy trials of those responsible for the July massacre in 2024.
key_facts: The NCP member secretary said the party would also participate in programmes organised by the 11-party alliance while maintaining its independent political identity.

Announcing the programme, NCP Member Secretary Akhtar Hossain said the party would organise a series of protest rallies and meetings in districts and metropolitan areas across the country from November to December.

He made the announcement at a press conference at the party's central office in the capital's Banglamotor area on Thursday, following a meeting of the NCP Political Council, its highest policymaking body, which discussed the current political situation.

title: মুসলমানের জন্য যে ৭ ধরনের পোশাক পরা নিষিদ্ধ
summary: পোশাক মানুষের সভ্যতা, সংস্কৃতি ও রুচির পরিচায়ক। ইসলামে কোনো নির্দিষ্ট দেশ বা সংস্কৃতির পোশাককে বাধ্যতামূলক করা হয়নি; বরং প্রতিটি অঞ্চলের মানুষ ইসলামের মূলনীতি মেনে নিজেদের ঐতিহ্যবাহী পোশাক পরতে পারেন। তবে শালীনতা রক্ষা, আত্মমর্যাদা বজায় রাখা এবং অহংকার বা অপচয় রোধ করার জন্য ইসলাম পোশাকের ক্ষেত্রে কিছু সুনির্দিষ্ট সীমারেখা টেনে দিয়েছে। যেসব পোশাক এই মূলনীতি লঙ্ঘন করে, মুসলমানদের জন্য সেগুলো পরিধান করা নিষিদ্ধ (হারাম বা মাকরুহ)। ১. আব্রু অনাবৃত রাখে এমন পোশাক পোশাকের প্রথম ও প্রধান উদ্দেশ্য হলো সতর (শরীরের আবশ্যিক ঢেকে রাখার অংশ) আবৃত করা। যে পোশাক পরলে সতর ঢাকে না—যেমন অতি সংক্ষিপ্ত পোশাক, খুব
key_facts: তারা বেহেশতে প্রবেশ করবে না, এমনকি বেহেশতের ঘ্রাণও পাবে না।’ (সহিহ মুসলিম, হাদিস: ২১২৮) ২.
মহানবী বলেছেন, ‘লুঙ্গি বা পোশাকের যে অংশ টাখনুর নিচে ঝুলে থাকবে, তা দোজখে যাবে।’ (সহিহ বুখারি, হাদিস: ৫৭৮৭) অহংকারবশত এটি করলে তা হারাম এবং অহংকার ছাড়া অভ্যাসগতভাবে করলে মাকরুহে তাহরিমি।

নবীজি (সা.) বলেছেন, ‘যে ব্যক্তি দুনিয়ায় প্রসিদ্ধি বা অহংকারের পোশাক পরবে, কেয়ামতের দিন আল্লাহ তাকে লাঞ্ছনার পোশাক পরাবেন।’ (সুনানে আবু দাউদ, হাদিস: ৪০২৯) যেমন ছিল চার ইমামের পোশাক-পরিচ্ছদ ও জীবনযাপন ৫.
মহানবী বলেছেন, ‘যে ব্যক্তি যে জাতির সাদৃশ্য অবলম্বন করবে, সে তাদেরই অন্তর্ভুক্ত বলে গণ্য হবে।’ (সুনানে আবু দাউদ, হাদিস: ৪০৩১) ৬.

title: এএফসির দুটি পুরস্কার জিতল বাফুফে
summary: এশিয়ান ফুটবলের নিয়ন্ত্রক সংস্থা এএফসির কাছ থেকে একসঙ্গে দুটি পুরস্কার পেয়েছে বাংলাদেশ ফুটবল ফেডারেশন (বাফুফে)। থাইল্যান্ডের ব্যাংককে বৃহস্পতিবার অনুষ্ঠিত এএফসি অ্যাওয়ার্ডস ২০২৬ অনুষ্ঠানে ‘মেম্বার অ্যাসোসিয়েশন অব দ্য ইয়ার’-এর রুবি ক্যাটাগরি এবং গ্রাসরুটস ফুটবলের সিলভার ক্যাটাগরিতে পুরস্কার জিতেছে বাংলাদেশ। বাফুফের পক্ষে পুরস্কার দুটি গ্রহণ করেন সংস্থাটির কার্যনির্বাহী কমিটির সদস্য মো. গোলাম গাউস। এ বছর এএফসির এই দুই পুরস্কারের জন্যই মনোনীত হয়েছিল বাফুফে। শেষ পর্যন্ত দুই বিভাগেই স্বীকৃতি পেয়েছে বাংলাদেশের ফুটবলের নিয়ন্ত্রক সংস্থাটি। ‘মেম্বার অ্যাসোসিয়েশন অব দ্য ইয়ার’ পুরস্কারে সদস্যদেশগুলোর ফুটব
key_facts: এ বছর এএফসির এই দুই পুরস্কারের জন্যই মনোনীত হয়েছিল বাফুফে।
শেষ পর্যন্ত দুই বিভাগেই স্বীকৃতি পেয়েছে বাংলাদেশের ফুটবলের নিয়ন্ত্রক সংস্থাটি।
‘মেম্বার অ্যাসোসিয়েশন অব দ্য ইয়ার’ পুরস্কারে সদস্যদেশগুলোর ফুটবলের সামগ্রিক উন্নয়ন কার্যক্রম ও সাফল্য বিবেচনা করে এএফসি।

title: Partex Group MD sent to jail in Purbachal plot corruption case
summary: Partex Group Managing Director Ashfaq Aziz Rubel. Photo: Courtesy A Dhaka court has sent Partex Group Managing Director Ashfaq Aziz Rubel to jail after rejecting his bail petition in a corruption case over the allocation of plots in the Rajuk Purbachal residential project. Rubel surrendered before the court of Dhaka Special Judge-9 Abdus Salam on 17 November and sought bail to appeal against his conviction.
key_facts: Saiful Islam Mithu, bench assistant of the court, confirmed the development yesterday (19 November).
On 13 October, the same court sentenced Rubel, his brother Shawkat Aziz Russell and six former Rajuk officials to 14 years in prison each in the corruption case.
Rubel and Russell were each sentenced to seven years' rigorous imprisonment under Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, and another seven years under Section 409 of the Penal Code.
They were also fined Tk10 lakh under each provision, with an additional year of rigorous imprisonment for each unpaid fine.

title: 72 Grameen Bank branches targeted in arson attacks
summary: Staff Correspondent Grameen Bank yesterday said 72 of its branches had faced arson attacks or attempted arson since November 10, affecting loans and financial opportunities for thousands of its members. In a press release, the bank expressed concern over the attacks, saying furniture, computers, important documents and CCTV equipment had been damaged, while some branches had been almost completely gutted.
key_facts: The attacks have allegedly been carried out by activists of the Awami League, whose political activities remain banned.
The bank appealed to people to help protect its branches, saying the attacks affected not only its infrastructure but also the livelihoods of thousands of members.
Grameen Bank also said it had never been involved in damaging any establishment.

title: World Children’s Day: The forgotten children
summary: A Abdullah Hel Bubun Abdullah Hel Bubun At an age when most children are busy with either schoolwork or playground games, 11-year-old Md Shamim spends his days collecting scrap metal on the streets of Dhaka. Like thousands of other street-connected children across Bangladesh, Shamim still imagines a future beyond poverty despite being shut out of school, stable housing and many of the opportunities that could help him get there.
key_facts: More than 7 in 10 street children (72.39 percent) hope to change their lives, according to the Survey on Street Children 2022, conducted by the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) and UNICEF among 7,200 children nationwide.
Published in 2023, the survey found that many want to secure better jobs, return to school or start small businesses.
A 2024 UNICEF report estimated that more than 3.4 million children in Bangladesh live or work on the streets without parental care.
With 58.7 million children aged 0-17 in the country, according to the 2022 Population and Housing Census, roughly one in every 17 children ends up on the streets.

title: ‘Keep Bangladeshi politics out of Britain’
summary: Bulbul Hasan Bulbul Hasan Jas Athwal Labour MP Jas Athwal has called for Bangladeshi politics to be kept out of Britain after violence erupted in his constituency of Ilford South in east London, warning that political rivalries and conflicts originating in Bangladesh have no place on British streets. “Bangladeshi politics has to be contained in Bangladesh because it hasn’t got any place here,” Athwal told The Daily Star.
key_facts: Athwal said this in the wake of attack on an NCP event in London by activists of Awami League, whose activities remain banned, on Monday night.
He said he raised the incident directly with Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband earlier in the day, showing him video footage of the violence.

But he stressed that violence spilling over from Bangladeshi politics was counterproductive and made it harder for British politicians to advocate for people and communities with links to the country.

title: Normalcy yet to return to RMG hubs
summary: Staff Correspondent Garment workers leave their workplaces at Bhogra Bypass in Gazipur after being sent home without starting their shifts yesterday. Amid ongoing unrest in the sector, many factories are sending workers home after taking morning attendance only.
key_facts: PHOTO: ANISUR RAHMAN Normalcy is yet be restored in the garment sector, with 194 factories enforcing the “no work, no pay” provision while production was halted in 147 other units yesterday amid unrest over workers’ demand for better pay.
The workers, demanding a monthly minimum wage increase from Tk 12,500 to Tk 30,000 for around three weeks, clashed with police during demonstrations in Ashulia, Savar, and Gazipur yesterday.
Amid the unrest, authorities yesterday declared a “general holiday” at 10 garment factories in Gazipur.
Mohammad Tariqul Islam, officer-in-charge of Ashulia Police Station, told The Daily Star that several factories in the area declared “holidays” around 12:30pm.

title: BNP, opposition move to counter AL on streets
summary: Staff Correspondent The ruling BNP and opposition parties are separately stepping up their street activities to counter the ousted Awami League amid recent incidents of arson, vandalism and violence. Although the AL’s political activities remain banned, recent violence involving its leaders and activists has heightened political tensions and raised concerns over law and order.
key_facts: Meanwhile, the Jamaat-e-Islami-led 11-party alliance has announced plans to take to the streets to “protect the country from defeated and hegemonic forces”.

Rizvi said the BNP would observe Martyred Intellectuals Day on December 14, Victory Day on December 16 and the first death anniversary of former prime minister and BNP chairperson Khaleda Zia on December 30.
The party will also celebrate the first anniversary of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s homecoming on December 25, marking his return in 2025 after years of exile.

Meanwhile, following a meeting of top leaders of the 11-party alliance at the opposition leader’s official residence on Minto Road yesterday, Bangladesh Khelafat Majlish Ameer Mamunul Haque said the alliance would remain active on the streets to resist attempts to create unrest.

title: Rohingya response must move beyond emergency aid
summary: At a policy dialogue in Dhaka yesterday, researchers called for moving beyond emergency relief by expanding access to education and livelihoods, investing in host communities, creating jobs for women, and improving access to information to prepare refugees for repatriation. The recommendations followed the unveiling of two BRAC studies involving 1,152 people aged 15 to 35, equally divided between Rohingya refugees and host community members in Ukhiya and Teknaf.
key_facts: It found that 66.7 percent of local youths believe the crisis has hurt their livelihoods, while 95.5 percent want government initiatives to create more jobs.

Carol Flore-Smereczniak, UN resident coordinator in Bangladesh, said the UN’s cooperation framework for 2028–2032 will link humanitarian assistance with longer-term investment in livelihoods, public services, environmental recovery and disaster resilience in Cox’s Bazar.
The dialogue, titled “Rohingya Crisis at Year Ten and Beyond: Rethinking the Response”, was held at a hotel in the capital.

title: A poet, a pioneer, a conscience for generations
summary: Staff Correspondent Sultana Kamal speaks at the memorial meeting. Photo: Star Rain had been falling across Dhaka for much of yesterday when family members, rights activists and admirers gathered at Sanjher Maya in Dhanmondi to pay tribute to poet and women’s rights pioneer Sufia Kamal on the eve of her 27th death anniversary, which falls today. For her daughter Sultana Kamal, the adverse weather reflected a wider sense of uncertainty in the country.
key_facts: Inside the Road 32 house, a large portrait of the poet hung against a backdrop of marigold garlands.
The house is named after her first poetry collection, published in 1938.
The poet’s portrait, she added, remains in the organisation’s offices across 56 districts, while pictures of political leaders changed with successive governments.
Born on June 20, 1911, in Shayestabad, Barishal, Sufia Kamal became a leading figure in Bangladesh’s literary, cultural, and women’s rights movements.

title: A safety net for journalists and rights defenders
summary: Staff Correspondent Journalists and human rights defenders can seek medical, legal and psychosocial support through a referral mechanism introduced by a project working on newsroom safety. The project, Swadhinata, or Freedom of Expression for Digital Democracy (FREEDOM), is funded by the European Union.
key_facts: The initiative was discussed at a two-day workshop organised by Breaking the Silence on November 18–19 at The Daily Star Centre, bringing together representatives of 20 media organisations, Manusher Jonno Foundation (MJF), Plan International Bangladesh and Plan International Netherlands.
The project also offers one-time cash assistance of Tk 19,180 to a total of 128 beneficiaries who have suffered serious work-related injuries.
Under the project, individuals will receive medical, legal, psychosocial and digital safety support from partner local organisations.

title: Malaysia job market reopening mired in uncertainty
summary: Mohammad Jamil Khan Mohammad Jamil Khan The government’s repeated assurances about resuming worker departures to Malaysia have been followed by shifting timelines, uncertainty over recruitment costs, and fresh medical requirements, raising questions about its preparedness to reopen the labour market. Although worker departures were expected to resume in the first week of November, the government is now targeting the end of the month.
key_facts: Meanwhile, the expatriates’ welfare and overseas employment ministry yesterday issued an 11-point directive for medical centres, nearly three weeks after announcing the start of medical tests and three days after declaring 51 centres operational for full-scale examinations.

On October 28, State Minister Nurul Haque Nur said recruitment procedures would be ready by November 1, allowing workers to leave within two to four days of medical examinations, subject to other formalities.
On November 5, Expatriates’ Welfare Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury said the government hoped to send the first two or three flights under its zero-cost recruitment initiative in December.
On November 12, BOESL Managing Director Mohammad Rashedul Haque said the agency was trying to send its first batch through DHL Supply Chain Malaysia before December.

title: Rough seas strand 1,500 tourists on St Martin’s
summary: Staff Correspondent, Cox’s Bazar Tourist vessel services on the Cox’s Bazar-St Martin’s route were suspended from yesterday until further notice, due to rough seas caused by Cyclone Akvan, leaving around 1,500 tourists stranded on the island. Additional District Magistrate Tasnim Jahan said services would resume depending on sea conditions.
key_facts: Hossain Islam Bahadur, general secretary of the Sea Cruise Operators Owners Association of Bangladesh, said around 1,500 tourists who travelled to the island on Tuesday and Wednesday could not return.
Vessel services on the route resumed on November 5, with five vessels permitted to operate this season.
A maximum of 3,500 tourists are allowed to visit the island daily.
Under government restrictions, tourist access to St Martin’s is permitted until March 15 next year, with overnight stays allowed.

title: Garment maker racks up Tk 169cr debt through LC fraud at Rupali
summary: The garment maker, Byzid Apparels (Pvt) Limited, had an approved back-to-back letter of credit (LC) limit of just Tk 8 crore. But officials at the bank’s Rupali Sadan Branch in Chattogram allegedly opened LCs worth far more without recording them in the lender’s core banking system (CBS), hiding the transactions from the head office and the central bank.
key_facts: The report says the irregularities took place between 2022 and 2024.
To understand how a Tk 8 crore limit turned into a Tk 169 crore liability, it helps to know how back-to-back LCs work.
In this case, however, Byzid Apparels failed to export against the LCs, leaving the bank with payment obligations of Tk 169 crore.
Byzid Apparels had been conducting import and export business through the branch since 2018.

title: New dollar declaration rule squeezes banks, travellers
summary: Ahsan Habib Ahsan Habib Md Zakir Hossain returned to Bangladesh from Thailand on November 11, unaware of a new Bangladesh Bank rule requiring returning passengers to declare their foreign currency cash at the airport. After covering all his expenses abroad, he brought back around $700.
key_facts: Under a Bangladesh Bank circular issued on November 9, foreign currency brought into the country by resident Bangladeshis can be credited to RFCD accounts only if it has been declared to customs using the Foreign Money and Jewellery (FMJ) form.
Previously, passengers could bring in up to $10,000 without making a customs declaration and deposit the money in an RFCD account without submitting an FMJ form.
Another option would have been to waive the customs declaration requirement for deposits of up to $5,000, he suggested.
Amid the cash dollar shortage, Bangladesh Bank sold around $220 million to scheduled banks yesterday to ease the pressure on foreign currency availability.

title: Renewables drive faces skilled worker shortage: survey
summary: Bangladesh’s ambition to expand renewable energy could be held back by a shortage of skilled workers, with 82 percent of surveyed firms reporting at least one vacancy that was difficult to fill, mainly for engineers and technicians, according to the South Asian Network on Economic Modeling (SANEM).
key_facts: PHOTO: Rashed Shumon Bangladesh’s ambition to expand renewable energy could be held back by a shortage of skilled workers, with 82 percent of surveyed firms reporting at least one vacancy that was difficult to fill, mainly for engineers and technicians, according to the South Asian Network on Economic Modeling (SANEM).
The think tank found that 86 percent of the 60 firms surveyed said candidates lacked practical skills and relevant experience, while 29 percent said they received too few applications.

In the keynote paper, Md Tuhin Ahmed, a lecturer in economics at Mawlana Bhashani Science and Technology University, estimated that Bangladesh would need around 1.55 lakh workers with short, certification-linked training and 75,000 STEM-qualified professionals in the renewable energy sector by 2035.
The projection comes as Bangladesh plans to add more than 10,000 megawatts of renewable energy capacity by 2030, almost five times its current installed capacity.

title: Bangladesh risks low-growth cycle, World Bank warns
summary: Rejaul Karim Byron Jagaran Chakma Rejaul Karim Byron and Jagaran Chakma Bangladesh risks remaining trapped in a low-growth cycle, with average economic growth projected at 4.2 percent over the decade to 2035 unless it undertakes reforms, the World Bank has warned. Sustained reforms, however, could lift average annual growth to 5.7 percent. This would add 1.5 percentage points to average annual growth, with the rate reaching 6.2 percent by fiscal year 2034-35.
key_facts: Under the reform scenario, domestic revenue could rise from 8 percent of GDP in FY25 to 14.4 percent by FY35, compared with 10 percent under the baseline scenario.
Tax revenue alone could reach 12.6 percent of GDP through VAT reforms, better compliance, stronger audits and enforcement, and a broader tax base.
The reform plan also calls for cutting subsidies by around 1.4 percentage points of GDP by FY35, making more funds available for development spending.
Total government expenditure could rise from 11.4 percent of GDP in FY25 to 18 percent by FY35.

title: Manufacturing sheds 14 lakh jobs despite output growth
summary: Star Business Report Bangladesh’s manufacturing output has grown by an average of 10 percent annually over the past decade, but the sector has lost a net 14 lakh jobs, according to a new analysis. Manufacturing employment fell from 95 lakh to 81 lakh despite sustained growth in industrial output, highlighting a widening disconnect between economic expansion and employment generation, the study found.
key_facts: The manufacturing sector’s share of total employment also declined from around 20 percent to 17 percent in 2023 over the decade, even as its contribution to gross domestic product increased, he said.

The trend poses a major challenge for Bangladesh, which needs to generate more than 20 lakh jobs annually amid widespread informality, skills mismatches and mounting pressure on the labour market, Razzaque said.
Between 2010 and 2023, garment exports more than tripled to $40 billion from $12.5 billion.
However, employment in the sector remained largely stagnant at around 40 lakh workers, according to Razzaque.

title: Germany pledges €246m in fresh funds
summary: Photo: Ministry of Finance Germany has committed up to €246 million in fresh development cooperation funds for Bangladesh, taking its total commitments since the 2024 intergovernmental negotiations to €402 million, or around Tk 5,507 crore. The country’s total development cooperation commitments to Bangladesh since 1972 have reached €3.9 billion, according to a press release issued yesterday.
key_facts: The latest pledges were finalised at the Bangladesh-Germany Development Cooperation Negotiations 2026, which concluded on Wednesday.
The talks were held in a hybrid format, following the first in-person round in Dhaka on October 27.

Shahriar thanked Germany for nearly 55 years of development cooperation and highlighted shared priorities, including poverty reduction, good governance, climate resilience, renewable energy and sustainable development.

title: Resolve economic issues, end corruption: Hossain Zillur
summary: Star Business Report Economist Hossain Zillur Rahman yesterday urged the government to resolve economic challenges while stopping corruption and harassment so entrepreneurs can expand their businesses. The economy is in a genuinely tough state for valid reasons, and the government needs to think about these issues but should not remain bogged down by them, he said.
key_facts: Zillur, a former adviser to the military-backed caretaker government, made the remarks while speaking as a conference speaker at the 20th annual general meeting of the International Business Forum of Bangladesh (IBFB) at Renaissance Dhaka.
He is also the chairperson of BRAC Bangladesh and executive chairman of the Power and Participation Research Centre (PPRC).
“People are moving forward with a mindset of building ‘my own destiny’.

title: BB expands farm credit to climate-smart agriculture
summary: Star Business Report The central bank has set an agricultural loan disbursement target of Tk 60,000 crore for FY27, up 54 percent from Tk 39,000 crore in FY26. The target aims to boost farm production, contain inflation and stimulate the rural economy. The photo was taken yesterday in Durgapur upazila of Rajshahi.
key_facts: Photo: Azahar Uddin Bangladesh Bank (BB) has revised its agricultural and rural credit policy for fiscal 2026-27, bringing precision farming, climate-smart agriculture and agricultural value chains under its scope.
The central bank’s Agricultural Credit Department amended the policy, originally issued on August 16, through a circular sent to all scheduled banks yesterday.
BB has set an agricultural loan disbursement target of Tk 60,000 crore for FY27, up 54 percent from Tk 39,000 crore in FY26.
Banks disbursed Tk 42,834 crore in FY26, exceeding that year’s target, according to BB data.

title: Bribery, now with a file number
summary: A man asked the peon at a government office how long his file would take. “Depends, sir,” came the reply. “Will the file walk, or take a rickshaw?” In our country, that rickshaw fare has kept pace with administrative reform. It began as “speed money”, paid to make a file move. Then it became mandatory, even when nothing moved faster. Now it is evolving into a gift, sometimes a documented one. We are not eliminating corruption; we are upgrading its vocabulary.
key_facts: GhushSite, launched on August 21, lets people anonymously report alleged bribe demands.
By September 13, it had received 18,899 complaints involving Tk 557.31 crore.
A 2025 household survey by Transparency International Bangladesh found that 63.6 percent of households had paid bribes, up from 50.8 percent in 2023, an estimated Tk 12,633 crore a year.
Our e-procurement system handled about 80 percent of public procurement spending in 2022, up from 2 percent in 2017, the World Bank reported.

title: কারিনার ফ্যাশন যেন ‘রাজায় রাজায় টক্কর’
summary: তিন দিনের ভারতীয় সফর শেষ করে যুক্তরাজ্যে ফিরে গেছেন প্রিন্স উইলিয়াম ও প্রিন্সেস অব ওয়েলস কেট মিডলটন । প্রিন্সের প্রতিষ্ঠিত পরিবেশবিষয়ক উদ্যোগ আর্থশট প্রাইজের ষষ্ঠ আয়োজন উপলক্ষে ভারতে এসেছিলেন তাঁরা। ১৬ থেকে ১৮ নভেম্বর ভারত সফরে কেট মিডলটন আলেকজান্ডার ম্যাককুইন ও রোকসান্ডার মতো ব্র্যান্ডের পোশাকের পাশাপাশি ভারতীয় ব্র্যান্ডের পোশাক ও গয়না পরেছেন। প্রিন্স উইলিয়ামকে দেখা গেছে নেহরু কোট থেকে মনিশ মালহোত্রার প্রিন্স কোটে। ব্রিটিশ রাজজুটির সঙ্গে বিভিন্ন আয়োজনে দেখা গেছে একাধিক বলিউড তারকাকে। তবে তাঁর মধ্যে সবাইকে ছাপিয়ে যেন রাজায় রাজায় টক্কর হলো কারিনা কাপুর ও সাইফ আলী খানের সঙ্গে। ভারতের বিখ্যাত পতৌ
key_facts: ভারতের বিখ্যাত পতৌদির নবাব পরিবারের প্রিন্স সাইফ আলী খান ও তাঁর স্ত্রী বলিউড অভিনেত্রী কারিনা কাপুরের সাজ ছিল বিশেষভাবে চোখে পড়ার মতো প্রথম আলোকে নির্ভরযোগ্য সূত্র হিসেবে পেতে হলে এখানে ক্লিক করুন ১ / ৯ সফরের শেষ দিন ১৮ নভেম্বর প্রিন্স উইলিয়াম গিয়েছিলেন বলিউডের বিখ্যাত প্রযোজনা প্রতিষ্ঠান ধর্মা প্রোডাকশনের অফিসে।

প্রিন্সকে স্বাগত জানাতে সেখানে উপস্থিত ছিলেন চলচ্চিত্র নির্মাতা করণ জোহর; অভিনয়শিল্পী দম্পতি কারিনা কাপুর খান ও সাইফ আলী খান এবং ধর্মা প্রোডাকশনসের সিইও অপূর্ব মেহতা ছবি: ইনস্টাগ্রাম থেকে ২ / ৯ প্রিন্সের সঙ্গে সাক্ষাতের সেই অনুষ্ঠানে সাইফ ও কারিনার পোশাক ছিল আইভরি রঙের।

তাঁর এই সাজ যেন মনে করিয়ে দিল, পাওয়ার ড্রেসিংয়ের জন্য সব সময় ফরমাল প্যান্টই জরুরি নয় ছবি: ইনস্টাগ্রাম থেকে আরও পড়ুন ভারতীয় ডিজাইনারের লাল আনারকলিতে নজর কাড়লেন ব্রিটিশ রাজবধূ কেট মিডলটন ৬ ঘণ্টা আগে ৫ / ৯ কারিনার পোশাকের ওপরের অংশে ছিল ডাবল ব্রেস্টেড জ্যাকেট।
চওড়া ল্যাপেল, স্ট্রং কাঁধের গড়ন ও ফ্ল্যাট পকেটের নিখুঁত কাটিং ছবি: ইনস্টাগ্রাম থেকে ৬ / ৯ তবে ব্লেজারের স্বতন্ত্র নকশার সঙ্গে সাজে নতুন মাত্রা যোগ করেছে একই রঙের মেঝে ছোঁয়া প্লিটেড স্কার্ট।

title: Myanmar found guilty of genocide. What happens now?
summary: (Photo: REUTERS/Piroschka van de Wouw) It does not get any more definitive than this. The world’s top court found Myanmar guilty of genocide. The UN court also found that it had failed to prevent or punish acts of genocide among other violations under the genocide convention.
key_facts: In the of Nicaragua vs USA, the ICJ had ruled in 1986 that the United States violated international law by mining Nicaraguan harbours and funding the Contra rebels.
Nicaragua invoked this security council provision where a draft resolution calling for the compliance of ICJ verdict got 11 votes, 3 abstentions and 1 veto.
Similarly, when in March 2022, the ICJ ordered Russia to suspend military operations in Ukraine, Russia ignored the order.
On this front, which is most crucial for Bangladesh -- over a million Rohingya have sought refuge here since 2017 -- things are unlikely to move.

title: Tarique’s birthday today
summary: UNB, Dhaka Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman turns 61 today, his first birthday since taking office as head of government in February. The eldest son of BNP founder and former president Ziaur Rahman and former prime minister Khaleda Zia, he was born on November 20, 1965, in Bogura. He grew up under the discipline of his father, an army officer who later became president.
key_facts: He formally entered politics in 1988, becoming a primary member of the BNP in Gabtali upazila of Bogura.
The party appointed him senior joint secretary general in 2002.

After his arrest in 2007 under the military-backed caretaker government, he went to London in 2008 for medical treatment and lived there with his family until returning to Bangladesh in December 2025.
He was elected the party’s senior vice-chairman in 2009.

title: Dhaka welcomes ICJ verdict
summary: Diplomatic Correspondent Bangladesh yesterday welcomed the International Court of Justice’s (ICJ) judgment holding Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya, saying it could have positive implications for the persecuted community and countries affected by the atrocities. “We welcome the ICJ verdict and are satisfied.
key_facts: For the first time in the history of international court proceedings, a state has been condemned for genocide,” State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir told reporters at the foreign ministry yesterday afternoon.
He said the ruling could benefit the Rohingya and countries affected by the atrocities, including Bangladesh, which hosts more than a million refugees who fled persecution in Myanmar.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam described the ruling as historic.

title: BB relaxes rules for Tk 60,000cr stimulus loans
summary: Staff Correspondent Bangladesh Bank has relaxed its rules on stimulus loans, allowing borrowers with court stay orders against default proceedings to access the Tk 60,000 crore package. The central bank issued a circular in this regard yesterday, effective immediately. Although the Bank Company Act bars fresh lending to defaulters, the directive allows borrowers to access the package if courts have stayed proceedings in cases or writ petitions they filed.
key_facts: All other provisions of the July 29 circular remain unchanged.
Announced in May to revive the private sector, the package had disbursed Tk 12,000 crore by mid-October, a fifth of its allocation.

Its 15 low-interest schemes cover closed industries, small businesses, agriculture, food security, export diversification, green industries, agro-based economic hubs, the creative economy, leather and frozen food exports.
Introduced in June, the one-time facility allows interest waivers and single-payment settlements for loans classified as “bad” or “loss” as of June 30, 2026.

title: ‘Enough is enough’
summary: Staff Correspondent Prime Minister Tarique Rahman addressing a rally in Lalmonirhat Sadar upazila yesterday. Photo: PMO Prime Minister Tarique Rahman yesterday called on democratic political parties and the people to unite against what he described as the ousted Awami League’s renewed politics of arson and violence, saying people no longer wanted the politics of arson, enforced disappearances and killings.
key_facts: He urged all democratic parties that fought for democracy during the 2024 uprising to stand together and prepare to resist those involved in violence, reports UNB.
“Let us all prepare ourselves once again, as we did in 2024, to give these terrorists a befitting response,” he said.
Tarique alleged that a group which had fled across the border after ruling the country by force for 16 years was again conspiring against Bangladesh.

“Let us all prepare ourselves once again, as we did in 2024, to give these terrorists a befitting response.” “Even after fleeing the country, they have once again started their politics of arson and killing people.

title: Myanmar committed Rohingya genocide
summary: Agencies Rohingyas celebrate the ICJ verdict at a camp in Cox’s Bazar yesterday. Photo: Reuters Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, the International Court of Justice said (ICJ) yesterday in an historic ruling, ordering refugees be given safe passage home and awarded compensation.
key_facts: The ruling by the top UN court was the first time in its 80-year history that ICJ judges have determined that a state committed genocide, and is likely to be seen as justice for Rohingya victims of Myanmar’s brutal 2017 crackdown.
Myanmar’s security forces killed some 10,000 Rohingya civilians, committed “widespread sexual violence” against women and “extreme violence” against children, Iwasawa said.

Genocide, defined after the Nazi Holocaust by a 1948 UN convention, is harder to prove than war crimes because it requires evidence of specific “intent” to destroy a national, ethnic, racial or religious group, reports The Guardian online.
He commanded the military during the Rohingya crackdown before ousting the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in a 2021 coup.

title: ‘We will be truly happy when we return home’
summary: Mokammel Shuvo Mokammel Shuvo Rohingya refugees watch the International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruling over whether Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya Muslims, on a screen at a camp in Bangladesh's Cox's Bazar on November 19, 2026. Photo: SALAHUDDIN AHMED / AFP Sadek Hossain, a Rohingya youth, cannot straighten his right leg since he was shot in the knee while fleeing a military crackdown in Myanmar in 2017.
key_facts: My right leg has become almost useless,” he told this correspondent at Camp 15 in Ukhiya, as thousands of Rohingya refugees nearby were watching the International Court of Justice (ICJ) proceedings on a large screen.
In 2017, Myanmar’s military set fire to Sadek’s village in Buthidaung, Rakhine State, forcing residents to flee.
Several refugees said around 10,000 people were killed in Rakhine during August and September 2017 and now it is proven.

For people like Sadek, who lost relatives and suffered injuries during the 2017 military crackdown, said the pain of losing family members and his own physical suffering would only ease when they could return home with international support.

title: Garment maker racks up Tk 169 crore debt through LC fraud at Rupali Bank
summary: A Chattogram-based garment maker has run up liabilities of more than Tk 169 crore at state-owned Rupali Bank, over 21 times its approved import financing limit, after branch officials allegedly bypassed the bank’s central accounting system, an internal audit has found.

title: Germany pledges €246 million in fresh funds
summary: Germany has committed up to €246 million in fresh development cooperation funds for Bangladesh, taking its total commitments since the 2024 intergovernmental negotiations to €402 million, or around Tk 5,507 crore.

title: নেত্রকোনায় ছাত্রশক্তি নেতা তালাত মাহমুদ রাফির বাড়িতে পেট্রল ঢেলে অগ্নিসংযোগ
summary: দুর্বৃত্তরা বাড়ির বিদ্যুতের মিটারের ঠিক নিচে পেট্রল ঢেলে আগুন ধরিয়ে দেয়। নেত্রকোনার মোহনগঞ্জ উপজেলার জয়পুর গ্রামে জাতীয় ছাত্রশক্তির জ্যেষ্ঠ যুগ্ম সাধারণ সম্পাদক ও বৈষম্যবিরোধী ছাত্র আন্দোলনের সমন্বয়ক খান তালাত মাহমুদ রাফির নেত্রকোনার মোহনগঞ্জ উপজেলার গ্রামের বাড়িতে আগুন দেওয়ার ঘটনা ঘটেছে। দুর্বৃত্তরা বাড়ির বিদ্যুতের মিটারের নিচে পেট্রল ঢেলে আগুন ধরিয়ে দেয়। এ সময় বাড়িতে ঘুমিয়ে ছিলেন রাফির বাবা-মা। প্রতিবেশীদের তৎপরতায় আগুন দ্রুত নেভানো সম্ভব হওয়ায় তাঁরা প্রাণে রক্ষা পান। গত বুধবার দিবাগত রাত সাড়ে তিনটার দিকে উপজেলার সমাজ সহিলদেও ইউনিয়নের জয়পুর গ্রামে এ ঘটনা ঘটে। খান তালাত মাহমুদের অভিযোগ, কার্য
key_facts: এ সময় বাড়িতে ঘুমিয়ে ছিলেন রাফির বাবা-মা।
প্রতিবেশীদের তৎপরতায় আগুন দ্রুত নেভানো সম্ভব হওয়ায় তাঁরা প্রাণে রক্ষা পান।
গত বুধবার দিবাগত রাত সাড়ে তিনটার দিকে উপজেলার সমাজ সহিলদেও ইউনিয়নের জয়পুর গ্রামে এ ঘটনা ঘটে।

title: 17 senior police officials transferred in major reshuffle, including two DIGs
summary: Photo: Collected The government has transferred 17 senior police officials in a major reshuffle, including two deputy inspectors general (DIGs), an additional DIG and several superintendents of police (SPs). The transfers were announced in a notification issued today (19 November) by the Home Ministry's Police-1 Branch, signed by Deputy Secretary Tousif Ahmed on behalf of the president.
key_facts: Mohammad Matiur Rahman Siddiqui, SP of Dhaka Police Telecom, has been transferred to the In-Service Training Centre of APBn-6 in Mahalchhari, Khagrachhari.

According to the notification, Mohammad Osman Gani, additional police commissioner (DIG) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), has been transferred to Rangpur Police Training Centre (PTC) as commandant.
Mohammad Mahiul Islam, deputy commissioner (DC) of Gazipur Metropolitan Police (GMP), has been posted to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) as a special superintendent of police (SP).

key_facts: প্রতি কেজি মাত্র ৮০০ টাকা।’ মাইকে একের পর এক এমন ঘোষণা এবং ব্যান্ড পার্টির বাদ্যযন্ত্রের তালে প্রচারণায় যোগ হয়েছে নতুনমাত্রা।
